summary: Grackle has no dedicated "mutation runtime" — GraphQL mutations are modelled as ordinary root fields on the schema's `Mutation` type whose field mappings are `RootEffect`s. A `RootEffect` is an `EffectMapping` that runs an effect `F[Result[(Query, Cursor)]]` before the normal result-construction stage: it performs the effectful write and then yields the (possibly rewritten) query plus a root cursor that the interpreter traverses to build the response. Three convenience constructors cover the common shapes: `RootEffect.computeUnit` (write, leave the query/cursor unchanged), `RootEffect.computeCursor` (write, supply a hand-built cursor — used by in-memory mappings), and `RootEffect.computeChild` (write, then rewrite the child query using data only known after the write, e.g. a freshly-inserted row id). Arguments reach the effect via the elaboration `Env` (populated in the `SelectElaborator` with `Elab.env(...)` and read with `env.getR[...]`). Mutations execute serially in client order within a single `runOneShot` pass; `RootEffect` and `RootStream` share machinery, with `RootStream` reserved for subscriptions. Grackle itself does not open or manage transactions — atomicity is entirely the responsibility of the user's effect (e.g. doobie `.transact(xa)` or a skunk session).

keyConcepts.name: RootEffect
keyConcepts.explanation: An `EffectMapping` field mapping placed on the schema's `Mutation` (or `Query`) object type. It wraps `effect: (Query, Path, Env) => F[Result[(Query, Cursor)]]`. The interpreter runs this effect first (the actual write), then traverses the returned cursor with the returned query to construct the JSON response. This is the entire mechanism behind GraphQL mutations in Grackle — there is no separate mutation API.

keyConcepts.name: computeUnit / computeCursor / computeChild
keyConcepts.explanation: The three convenience constructors on `object RootEffect`. `computeUnit` runs an `Env => F[Result[Unit]]` effect and reuses the default root cursor with the unmodified (elaborated) query — used when the elaborator already rewrote the query (e.g. an UPDATE keyed on an id supplied as an argument). `computeChild` runs `(Query, Path, Env) => F[Result[Query]]`, letting you rewrite the child query *after* the effect — essential when the row id only exists post-INSERT. `computeCursor` runs `(Path, Env) => F[Result[Cursor]]` and supplies a hand-built cursor (e.g. `valueCursor`), used by in-memory ValueMappings and subscriptions.

keyConcepts.name: Env-based argument passing
keyConcepts.explanation: Mutation arguments are not passed directly to the effect. Instead the `SelectElaborator` captures them into the elaboration environment with `Elab.env(name, value)`; the value is later retrieved inside the `RootEffect` body with `env.getR[T](name)` (a `Result[T]`) or `env.get[T](name)` (an `Option[T]`). The interpreter merges per-node environments into the effect's `Env` via `rootCursor.fullEnv.addFromQuery(query)`.

keyConcepts.name: Two-phase elaboration for inserts
keyConcepts.explanation: For an UPDATE the client query can be fully elaborated up front (the `id` is an argument), so `computeUnit` + an elaborator `transformChild` that adds `Unique(Filter(Eql(.../"id", Const(id)), child))` suffices. For an INSERT the new row's `id` is unknown until the write runs, so the query rewrite must happen *inside* the effect via `computeChild`, which returns `Unique(Filter(Eql(CityType / "id", Const(id)), child)).success` using the id returned by the INSERT.

keyConcepts.name: Serial execution of mutation roots
keyConcepts.explanation: In `QueryInterpreter.runOneShot`, ungrouped root selections are partitioned into effectful (RootEffect-backed) and pure queries. Effectful queries are run with `effectfulQueries.traverse { ... }`, which for `F = IO` executes them sequentially in client order — matching the GraphQL spec requirement that top-level mutation fields run serially (verified by the 'serial execution' test). Results are merged with `|+|`.

keyConcepts.name: Transactions are the user's responsibility
keyConcepts.explanation: Grackle does not begin/commit transactions around a mutation. The `RootEffect` effect value is whatever the user supplies; the doobie test wraps each write in `.transact(transactor)` and the skunk test uses `pool.use(_.prepareR(...))`. Atomicity across the write and the subsequent read-back is therefore not guaranteed by Grackle and must be arranged by the user if required.

keyConcepts.name: RootStream vs RootEffect
keyConcepts.explanation: `RootStream` is the streaming sibling of `RootEffect` (effect type returns `Stream[F, Result[(Query, Cursor)]]`) and is only permitted in subscriptions; `runOneShot` returns an internal error if a `RootStream` appears in a non-subscription. A `RootEffect` can be lifted to a single-element stream via `toRootStream`, which is how subscriptions fall back to a plain effect when no explicit `RootStream` is defined.

keyTypes.name: RootEffect
keyTypes.signature: case class RootEffect private (fieldName: String, effect: (Query, Path, Env) => F[Result[(Query, Cursor)]])(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends EffectMapping { def hidden = false; def toRootStream: RootStream = RootStream(fieldName)((q, p, e) => Stream.eval(effect(q, p, e))) }
keyTypes.purpose: The field mapping that backs a GraphQL mutation root field. Runs an effect (the write) before result construction and yields the effective query plus root cursor. Constructor is private; use the companion's factory methods.

keyTypes.name: RootEffect.apply
keyTypes.signature: def apply(fieldName: String)(effect: (Query, Path, Env) => F[Result[(Query, Cursor)]])(implicit pos: SourcePos, di: DummyImplicit): RootEffect
keyTypes.purpose: Most general constructor: you compute BOTH the effective query and its root cursor yourself.

keyTypes.name: RootEffect.computeUnit
keyTypes.signature: def computeUnit(fieldName: String)(effect: Env => F[Result[Unit]])(implicit pos: SourcePos): RootEffect
keyTypes.purpose: Perform a side-effecting write that needs no data fed back into the query; the elaborated query and the default root cursor are used unchanged. Used for the UPDATE case where the elaborator already added the id filter.

keyTypes.name: RootEffect.computeCursor
keyTypes.signature: def computeCursor(fieldName: String)(effect: (Path, Env) => F[Result[Cursor]])(implicit pos: SourcePos): RootEffect
keyTypes.purpose: Perform a write and supply a hand-built root cursor (e.g. `valueCursor`) while leaving the client query unmodified. Used by in-memory ValueMappings and as the put-handler in SubscriptionSuite.

keyTypes.name: RootEffect.computeChild
keyTypes.signature: def computeChild(fieldName: String)(effect: (Query, Path, Env) => F[Result[Query]])(implicit pos: SourcePos): RootEffect
keyTypes.purpose: Perform a write and then rewrite the child query using data only available after the effect runs (e.g. the id of an inserted row). Executes against the default root cursor for the mapping.

keyTypes.name: EffectMapping
keyTypes.signature: trait EffectMapping extends FieldMapping { def subtree: Boolean = true }
keyTypes.purpose: Abstract base of field mappings with effects; `RootEffect`, `RootStream` and `EffectField` extend it. `subtree = true` means the mapping owns the whole subtree below the field.

keyTypes.name: RootStream
keyTypes.signature: case class RootStream private (fieldName: String, effect: (Query, Path, Env) => Stream[F, Result[(Query, Cursor)]])(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends EffectMapping { def hidden = false }
keyTypes.purpose: Streaming counterpart of RootEffect, used for subscriptions only. A RootEffect can be lifted via `toRootStream`.

keyTypes.name: Env
keyTypes.signature: sealed trait Env { def add[T](items: (String, T)*): Env; def add(env: Env): Env; def contains(name: String): Boolean; def get[T: ClassTag](name: String): Option[T]; def isEmpty: Boolean; def getR[A: ClassTag: TypeName](name: String): Result[A] = get[A](name).toResultOrError(s"Key '$name' of type ${typeName[A]} was not found in $this"); def addFromQuery(query: Query): Env }
keyTypes.purpose: The environment used to thread mutation arguments from the elaborator (`Elab.env`) into the RootEffect body (`env.getR` / `env.get`). `getR` yields a `Result` with a 'Key ... was not found' error if absent.

keyTypes.name: Elab.env
keyTypes.signature: def env(nme: String, value: Any): Elab[Unit]  /* also: env(kv, kvs*), env(kvs: Seq), env(other: Env), and env[T: ClassTag](nme): Elab[Option[T]] */
keyTypes.purpose: Called inside a SelectElaborator to bind a mutation's arguments into the elaboration environment so the RootEffect can read them later.

keyTypes.name: Elab.transformChild
keyTypes.signature: def transformChild(f: Query => Query)(implicit dummy: DummyImplicit): Elab[Unit]  /* also: f: Query => Elab[Query] and f: Query => Result[Query] */
keyTypes.purpose: Used in the UPDATE path to rewrite the child query at elaboration time (wrapping it in `Unique(Filter(Eql(CityType / "id", Const(id)), child))`).

keyTypes.name: Query.extractChild / substChild
keyTypes.signature: def extractChild(query: Query): Option[Query]   /* and */   def substChild(query: Query, newChild: Query): Option[Query]
keyTypes.purpose: computeChild internally calls extractChild to get the selection set under the mutation field, hands it to your effect, then substChild splices your rewritten child back in. If the root query has an unexpected shape these yield 'Root query has unexpected shape' errors.

keyTypes.name: Mapping.rootEffect
keyTypes.signature: def rootEffect(context: Context, fieldName: String): Option[RootEffect] = typeMappings.fieldMapping(context, fieldName).collect { case re: RootEffect => re }
keyTypes.purpose: How the interpreter discovers whether a given root field is effectful (i.e. a mutation).

keyTypes.name: Mapping.compileAndRun
keyTypes.signature: def compileAndRun(text: String, name: Option[String] = None, untypedVars: Option[Json] = None, introspectionLevel: IntrospectionLevel = Full, reportUnused: Boolean = true, env: Env = Env.empty)(implicit sc: Compiler[F, F]): F[Json]
keyTypes.purpose: The single entry point used by every mutation test to compile and execute a `mutation { ... }` document and get back `F[Json]`.

minimalExamples.title: In-memory mutation with RootEffect.computeCursor (no DB)
minimalExamples.explanation: Verbatim-equivalent to SubscriptionSuite. Shows the full pattern with zero database: the elaborator captures the `n` argument into the Env with `Elab.env`, the RootEffect reads it with `env.get[Int]`, performs the write (`ref.set`), and returns a `valueCursor` carrying the value to render. `Elab.env("n" -> n)` is the tuple-pair overload.

minimalExamples.title: SQL UPDATE mutation: RootEffect.computeUnit + elaborator transformChild
minimalExamples.explanation: From SqlMutationMapping.scala + DoobiePgSuites.scala. Because the `id` is a client argument, the query that reads the row back can be fully elaborated up front via `transformChild`, so the effect only has to perform the write and can use `computeUnit` (the elaborated query + default root cursor are reused). `env.getR[UpdatePopulation](...)` returns a `Result` and is sequenced with `.traverse`. The transaction is the user's `.transact(transactor)`, not Grackle's.

minimalExamples.title: SQL INSERT mutation: RootEffect.computeChild (id known only after the write)
minimalExamples.explanation: From SqlMutationMapping.scala + DoobiePgSuites.scala. This is the canonical computeChild case: the inserted row's `id` doesn't exist until the INSERT runs, so the read-back query must be built inside the effect. `computeChild` gives you the `child` selection set; you return `Unique(Filter(Eql(CityType / "id", Const(id)), child)).success` and Grackle splices it back and runs it against the default root cursor. `.flatTraverse` flattens the `Result[Result[Query]]` produced by combining `getR` and the effect.

minimalExamples.title: Driving an insert mutation end-to-end (the actual test)
minimalExamples.explanation: From SqlMutationSuite.scala. Demonstrates that a single `compileAndRun` both performs the write and returns the requested selection set of the newly written row — including a join back to `country` — proving the read-back query is executed against live data produced by the effect.

gotchas: RootEffect's case-class constructor is private. You MUST use the companion factories (`RootEffect.apply`, `computeUnit`, `computeCursor`, `computeChild`) — you cannot `new RootEffect(...)` from user code.

Arguments are NOT passed to the effect directly. They flow through the elaboration Env: bind them in the `SelectElaborator` with `Elab.env(name, value)` and read them in the effect with `env.getR[T](name)` / `env.get[T](name)`. Forgetting the `Elab.env` step makes `env.getR` fail at runtime with 'Key ... of type ... was not found'.

Choosing the wrong constructor for inserts: for an UPDATE keyed on an argument you can elaborate the read-back query up front (`computeUnit` + `transformChild`), but for an INSERT whose id is generated by the DB you MUST use `computeChild` and rewrite the query inside the effect — the id does not exist at elaboration time. The test comments call this out explicitly ('the query must be elaborated *after* execution of the effect').

Grackle does not manage transactions. There is no implicit transaction wrapping the write plus the subsequent read-back. The doobie tests use `.transact(transactor)` per statement and the skunk tests use `pool.use(...)`; if you need the write and read-back to be atomic you must arrange that yourself. The two halves can run on different connections/transactions.

computeChild requires the root query to have a recognisable shape. Internally it uses `Query.extractChild` / `Query.substChild`; if the top-level selection isn't a plain `Select`/`UntypedSelect` (optionally wrapped in `Environment`/`TransformCursor`) you get 'Root query has unexpected shape' errors.

`RootStream` is rejected outside subscriptions: `runOneShot` returns 'RootStream only permitted in subscriptions', and conversely subscriptions require an `EffectMapping` ('EffectMapping required for subscriptions'). Don't put a `RootStream` on the Mutation type.

Top-level mutation fields execute serially in client order (per the GraphQL spec). This is implied by `effectfulQueries.traverse` in `runOneShot` and is asserted by the 'serial execution' test (one:put / two:put / three:put leaves the ref at 3). Do not assume parallelism between sibling mutation roots.

`env.getR[T]` returns a `Result[T]` (an error value), not a thrown exception, when the key/type is missing — so you must sequence it (`.traverse`/`.flatTraverse`) rather than pattern-matching as if it were the raw value. `env.get[T]` returns `Option[T]` and silently yields `None` on type mismatch (it uses `classTag[T].unapply`).

The SQL mutation tests deliberately operate on a *copy* table `city_copy` (created via `CREATE TABLE city_copy AS SELECT * FROM city` and dropped afterwards) so the writes don't corrupt the shared read-only `city` fixture. The TableDef is `TableDef("city_copy")` while the GraphQL type is still `City`.

`computeCursor` leaves the client query unmodified, so any data produced by the effect can only reach result construction via the cursor's environment (`qc.map(_.withEnv(env))` / `valueCursor(path, env, value)`). If you build a cursor that doesn't carry the written value, the response won't reflect it.
